about.title: Menifee Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A fall can change an ordinary errand in Menifee into months of recovery. Whether it happened in a grocery store off Newport Road, an apartment stairwell near Murrieta Road, or a parking lot along Scott Road, California premises liability law asks one central question: did the property owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard and fail to fix it or warn you? That element, called notice, is where most of these claims are won or lost. Wet floors, uneven walkways, poor lighting, and loose handrails rarely leave much evidence behind once they are cleaned up or repaired, so acting early matters. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Menifee residents and visitors with an independent personal injury attorney who handles premises cases in Riverside County and works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened; we handle the introduction. From there, the attorney can help you gather photos, request surveillance footage, and keep the two-year filing deadline in view.

whyChoose.title: Why Menifee Fall Victims Start With LawProactive

items.title: Notice is the whole case, and we know it
items.desc: California requires proof the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorneys we connect you with focus early on how long the spill, crack, or broken step was there and who was responsible for checking.

items.title: Video disappears fast
items.desc: Many Menifee stores and complexes overwrite surveillance footage within days. A prompt preservation request from an attorney can keep the recording of your fall from being erased.

items.title: Partial fault doesn't shut the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly to blame, with your share reduced accordingly. Missing a warning sign or wearing the wrong shoes is not an automatic loss.

items.question: I fell on a cracked sidewalk maintained by the City of Menifee. Is the deadline different?
items.answer: Yes, and it matters a great deal. Claims against a public entity like the City of Menifee or Riverside County generally require a formal government claim within six months, which is far shorter than the two-year deadline for private property owners. Because those windows close quickly, it helps to speak with an attorney soon after the fall so the correct claim goes to the correct agency.

items.question: The store manager said I should have been watching where I was walking. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: Not by itself. California applies pure comparative fault, so a jury or insurer may assign you some percentage of blame and reduce your recovery by that amount, but a share of fault does not bar the claim. What still has to be shown is that the store knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to correct it or warn you.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a slip and fall in Menifee?
items.answer: Get medical care first, even if the pain seems minor, because fall injuries often worsen over the following days. Then photograph the exact spot, note the lighting and any signs, and write down the names of anyone who saw what happened. Ask the property for an incident report and request that surveillance video be preserved; an attorney can send that request in writing so it carries weight.
